A transformer is a neural network that uses self attention to relate every token in a sequence to every other token.
Attention lets each token look at other tokens and mix in the information that is most relevant to it.
A token is a small chunk of text, usually part of a word, that the model reads and predicts.
An epoch is one full pass of the training loop over every example in your dataset.
The learning rate controls how large a step the optimizer takes at each update. The default is 0.0003.
Overfitting is when the model memorizes the training data and stops improving on data it has not seen.
Temperature scales the logits before sampling. Lower values are more focused, higher values are more random.
Top p sampling keeps only the most likely tokens whose probabilities add up to p.
Top k sampling keeps only the k most likely tokens at each step.
A key value cache stores past attention keys and values so generation does not recompute the whole sequence each step.
Rotary position embedding encodes positions by rotating the query and key vectors, which gives the model relative position information.
RMSNorm normalizes a vector by its root mean square. It is cheaper than layer normalization and works well in low precision.
SwiGLU is a gated feed forward layer that multiplies a SiLU activated projection with a second linear projection.
Cross entropy measures how surprised the model is by the correct next token. Lower is better.
Perplexity is the exponential of the loss. It is roughly how many options the model is choosing between.
Gradient accumulation sums gradients over several small batches so you get the effect of a large batch in little memory.
A validation split is a slice of the data held out from training so you can measure how well the model generalizes.
